reflection.theme: The Ordinary Miracle of a Monday
reflection.quote: The most regretful people on earth are those who felt the call to creative work, who felt their own creative power restive and uprising, and gave to it neither power nor time.
reflection.reading:
Monday in August. The summer is doing that thing where it starts to tip — mornings a little cooler, the light already changing angle. If you're new to this, Mondays used to be the reckoning. The hangover audit. The what-did-I-say, what-did-I-spend, who-am-I-avoiding. A whole day spent trying to feel human again, and by the time you did, it was Wednesday.

Sober Mondays are almost boring by comparison, and that's the point. You wake up and the day is just a day. Coffee tastes like coffee. You answer the email. You go for the run you said you'd go for, or you don't, but the choice is actually yours. Mary Oliver was writing about creative work, but I think it applies here too — the regret isn't about the wild nights. It's about the mornings you gave away, the power and time you handed over to something that never gave anything back.

What sobriety keeps offering, quietly, is Monday. Just Monday. The chance to show up for an ordinary day and let it be ordinary. That's not a smaller life. That's the raw material of every good thing you'll ever build. The trips, the friendships, the seasons in the mountains — they all get scheduled on Mondays.
reflection.meditation: Today, notice one ordinary moment and let it be enough. The coffee. The walk to your car. A text from someone who knows you sober. That's the life.

affirmations: I am building a life on ordinary days, not just big moments.
Today I get to choose what I do with my time, and that choice is mine.
I am someone who shows up — for the small things, for the people who count on me, for myself.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful today for a quiet Monday morning — the kind I used to dread and now barely notice, which is its own kind of miracle. Grateful for coffee that tastes like coffee, for a clear head, for the people in my life who've only ever known me sober. And grateful for whoever is reading this on day one, day ninety, or year twelve — you're the reason any of this matters.
gratitude.closing: One ordinary day at a time.
